src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2022_us_sldu_500k
sldu.vint: The Census Bureau's 2022 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2022 legislative session year.
rec: 2021 plan: 83 Del. Laws c. 258 (SB 199, signed Nov. 2, 2021) as revised by c. 285 (HB 335, signed Apr. 1, 2022); 21 Senate districts
83 Del. Laws, c. 258 (SB 199, 151st General Assembly): reapportionment of the state legislative districts; signed 11/2/21

Two versions of the plan exist before the Nov. 2022 election: SB 199 (final maps Oct. 2021) and HB 335's revision (final maps March 2022, effective Apr. 1, 2022), which moves small areas only. The cb_2022 sldu file (LSY 2022, made April 2023) could hold either: 20 of 21 areas differ from the 2020 file by more than 0.5 percent (up to 38 percent), so it is a post-2020 plan, but its areas agree with the 2024 file to within 0.3 percent, which is no finer than the noise between years for states whose plan did not change, so the two versions cannot be told apart. Either way the picture is the same to the eye.

src: U.S. Census Bureau, cartographic boundary file cb_2022_us_sldl_500k
sldl.vint: The Census Bureau's 2022 file of legislative districts, the lines it records for the 2022 legislative session year.
rec: 2021 plan: 83 Del. Laws c. 258 (SB 199, signed Nov. 2, 2021) as revised by c. 285 (HB 335, signed Apr. 1, 2022); 41 House districts
83 Del. Laws, c. 258 (SB 199, 151st General Assembly): reapportionment of the state legislative districts; signed 11/2/21

As for the Senate: SB 199 and HB 335's small revision cannot be told apart in the cb_2022 sldl file (LSY 2022): 38 of 41 areas differ from the 2020 file by more than 0.5 percent (up to 73 percent) and agree with the 2024 file to within 0.05 percent.
